transcript.content:
hey, i'm Berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hi Berry. ok so the bit that's stuck with me is our old cat Biscuit, she was huge, like the size of a bus, because i'd shrunk down to about the size of a mouse. i was standing in the grass in my mum's back garden and it was taller than me

and the whole thing looked like a drawing i did in crayon when i was six, which was weird

oh Biscuit the size of a bus, and you down in the grass like a mouse

what was she doing?

she came through the grass towards me and picked me up really gently by the back of my jumper, like how cats carry kittens. then she climbed up the drainpipe onto the roof of the house with me hanging there

wasn't scary though, weirdly

carried up the drainpipe by the scruff of your jumper, dangling there, and not even scared

what happened once she got you up on the roof?

from the roof i could see all the gardens down our street, and there was a cat sitting in every single one. dozens of them, all sitting really still, all looking up at us

then Biscuit put me down on the roof tiles, they were warm, and she lay down next to me. and that was it, that's where it ended

a cat in every single garden, dozens of them, all sitting really still and looking up at you two

what was it like, being looked at by all of them?
honestly i don't really remember feeling anything specific about it. they were just all there looking up at us, really still. i don't remember being scared or anything

that's fine, sometimes they're just there

you said the roof tiles were warm and Biscuit lay down next to you. how did that bit feel, lying there with her at the end?
i don't really remember how it felt tbh. the dream doesn't go much further than that, she just lay down next to me on the warm tiles and then it ended

that's ok, that's where it stops

so you were in your mum's back garden, shrunk down to the size of a mouse, with the grass taller than you. Biscuit was huge, like the size of a bus, and she came through the grass towards you and picked you up really gently by the back of your jumper, the way cats carry kittens. she climbed up the drainpipe onto the roof with you hanging there, and it wasn't scary, weirdly. from the roof you could see all the gardens down your street, with a cat in every one, dozens of them, sitting really still and looking up at you both. then she put you down on the warm roof tiles and lay down next to you, and that's where it ended. and the whole thing looked like a crayon drawing you did when you were six

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's pretty much it! only things i'd add, Biscuit was ginger with one white ear, and the crayon look was like thick waxy lines with the colours going over the edges. otherwise spot on

ah, so Biscuit was ginger with one white ear, and the crayon look was thick waxy lines with the colours going over the edges

have i got that bit right now?
yep that's it, you've got it now

lovely, i've got Biscuit and her white ear now

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah i'd love that actually

here are a few ways it could be drawn: soft chalk pastels, gentle and dusty like a quiet afternoon nobody hurries. or like a page from a favourite bedtime book, cosy and matter-of-fact. or coloured pencils, quiet and careful, like someone drew it so it wouldn't move. or a child's crayon drawing, exactly like one you did at six, stuck on the fridge

which feels closest, or would you rather describe it your own way?
the crayon one, definitely. that's exactly how it looked

crayon it is. i'll start with your mum's back garden

i'm picturing it as the lawn out the back of her house, outdoors. my guesses: grass way taller than you, the back wall of the house with a drainpipe running up to the roof, and daylight

anything different from how you remember it, or shall i just go with that?
yeah that sounds right. grass taller than me, drainpipe going up to the roof, yep. i don't really remember what time of day it was, so just go with daylight

ok, i'm sketching your mum's back garden, Biscuit and the roof of the house now. it'll show up on the right

as for you, i'm picturing you in a jumper, since that's what Biscuit carried you by

anything different about how you looked, or would you leave that to me?
yeah a jumper's right. i don't remember what colour it was or anything else about how i looked though, so just go with whatever you think

ok, i'll pick the jumper for you

i'm sketching you now. everything's being drawn and it'll show up on the right over the next minute or two

if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
oh wow they're all up. yeah that looks right, that's really how it looked. Biscuit with her white ear and everything

oh good, Biscuit with her one white ear, up there with you on the warm tiles

if anything starts to look off the longer you look at it, just tell me
will do. honestly it looks just like it did, thanks Berry. nice seeing Biscuit again tbh

i'm really glad she came out like that, big and ginger with her one white ear, lying next to you on the warm tiles

it's nice to see her again
yeah it really is. she was a good cat. thanks for doing this, i might show my mum

she sounds like she was a really good cat

and your mum would probably love seeing her garden with Biscuit up on the roof like that
yeah i think she would, she loved that cat too. anyway thanks again Berry, this was really nice

thank you for bringing her back for a bit

i hope your mum gets a smile out of seeing Biscuit again, curled up next to you on those warm tiles

turns.brief:
Move: open_ended. Nothing to chase. Let them lead.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: still telling — follow what they raised
turns.brief:
Move: explore_thread → hi Berry. ok so the bit that's stuck with me is our old cat Biscuit, she was huge, like the size of a bus, because i'd shrunk down to about the size of a mouse.. Be curious about it: ask one thing about it, in their words, never suggesting what happened.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: still telling — follow what they raised
turns.brief:
Move: explore_thread → she came through the grass towards me and picked me up really gently by the back of my jumper, like how cats carry kittens. then she climbed up the drainpipe on. Be curious about it: ask one thing about it, in their words, never suggesting what happened.
</brief>

Move: explore_thread → from the roof i could see all the gardens down our street, and there was a cat sitting in every single one. dozens of them, all sitting really still, all lookin. Be curious about it: ask one thing about it, in their words, never suggesting what happened.
</brief>

Move: probe_goal → how it felt. What we'd like to know: the feeling of the dream, and whether it changed along the way. Ask it plainly, as curiosity, hung off something they said in their own words (never words of yours, and never say they said something they did not). If they don't remember, that's fine.
</brief>

Move: retell. You have their dream. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right or missed anything.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: take_correction. They changed or added something. In a sentence or two, tell back just that part the way they put it, then check you have it right now. Don't retell the whole dream, and don't say goodbye.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: offer_visualize. They've confirmed you have their dream. Ask them, simply and warmly, whether they'd like to see it drawn. One question. Don't explain how it works.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: O1: they want to see it
turns.brief:
Move: choose_style. They want to see it. Offer these ways it could be drawn, each in a few plain words, and ask which feels closest, or whether they'd describe their own: a) soft chalk pastels: Gentle and dusty, like a quiet afternoon that nobody hurries.; b) a picture book painting: Like a page from a favourite bedtime book, cosy and matter-of-fact.; c) a coloured pencil drawing: Quiet and careful, like someone drew the moment so it wouldn't move.; d) a child's crayon drawing: Exactly like a drawing you did at six, stuck on the fridge..
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: S1: they chose how it looks
turns.brief:
Move: start. They chose a child's crayon drawing. Say you'll start with mum's back garden, then describe how you picture mum's back garden on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: what kind of place: the back garden of the dreamer's mum's house, outdoors, a lawn in front of the back of the house. You filled in (say plainly that these are your guesses): what's in it: grass taller than the dreamer, the back wall of the house with a drainpipe running up to the roof; light: daylight. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: confirm_profile. First say, in a few words, that you're sketching mum's back garden and biscuit and the roof of the house now and it'll appear on the right: only that, nothing else is being drawn yet. Then describe how you picture you on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: wears: a jumper. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: B1: profile you_choose — all profiles settled
turns.brief:
Move: build_done. Say you're sketching you now. Tell them everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. They can say if anything looks wrong once it's there. Keep it short; no question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. biscuit and the cats in the gardens and mum's back garden and the roof of the house and you are up on the right now: ask if it looks the way they remember.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. Take in that they're happy with biscuit and the roof of the house. The rest are still on their way; if they ask, say they'll appear on the right soon.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. The rest are still on their way; if they ask, say they'll appear on the right soon.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: wrap. Something genuinely good came out of this for them. Send them off on it, and let that be the last thing they read. Do not ask another question.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

colours.value: bright crayon colours, like a drawing the dreamer did at six, the colours going over the edges of the lines

light.value: flat, even daylight, as in a child's drawing

texture.value: thick waxy crayon lines, colour scribbled past the edges, paper showing through

distinctive_features.value: one white ear; size as big as a bus

geography.value: the back garden of the dreamer's mum's house, outdoors, a lawn in front of the back of the house

landmarks.value: grass taller than the dreamer, the back wall of the house with a drainpipe running up to the roof

geography.value: the sloping tiled roof of mum's house, high above the gardens of the street

moments.action: The dreamer, the size of a mouse, stands in the back garden grass, which is taller than they are.
Biscuit, as big as a bus, comes through the grass towards the dreamer.
Biscuit picks the dreamer up very gently by the back of their jumper, the way cats carry kittens.
Biscuit climbs up the drainpipe towards the roof, the dreamer hanging from her mouth.
From the roof, the gardens down the street spread out below, a cat sitting very still in every one, all looking up at the dreamer and Biscuit.
Biscuit puts the dreamer down on the warm roof tiles.
Biscuit lies down on the roof next to the dreamer.

appearance.value: large adult ginger cat with short thick orange fur, plump build

geography.value: a small rectangular back garden of a house, outdoors: the back wall of the house runs along the far side, a lawn of very tall grass fills the middle, and low wooden fences run along both sides and the near edge

landmarks.value: very tall grass stalks, taller than a mouse-sized person; the red-brick back wall of a two-storey house with a door and windows; a grey drainpipe running straight up the wall to a sloping red-tiled roof; wooden fences around the edges

geography.value: a wide sloping rooftop of an ordinary house, rows of overlapping red clay roof tiles running up to a straight ridge at the top, a gutter along the lower edge, sun-warmed tiles

landmarks.value: a square red-brick chimney with an orange pot near the ridge, a white plastic gutter along the bottom edge, the top of a drainpipe curling over the gutter at one corner, open blue sky above

light.value: warm, bright daylight across the tiles

appearance.value: short brown hair worn casually, average build
